screening_decisions.reason: RCT in 50 women with stress urinary incontinence. PFM exercises (digital palpation) and biofeedback groups both constitute PFMT; the third arm received no exercises. Inactive control present.
RCT in 123 women with SUI. The app‐based intervention delivered PFMT (98.4% adherence); the control group received postponed treatment (waiting list, inactive). Meets all criteria.
RCT in 49 postmenopausal women with SUI. PFME alone arm versus a no‑treatment control. PFMT vs inactive control present.
RCT in 197 older women with urge/mixed UI. Biofeedback‑assisted behavioral treatment (includes PFMT) versus a placebo control. Inactive control arm exists.
RCT in 135 older women with sphincteric incompetence (stress UI). Pelvic muscle exercise group versus a no‑treatment control. PFMT vs inactive control.
RCT in 107 women with urodynamic stress incontinence. Pelvic floor exercises (PFMT) versus an untreated control group, among other arms. Inactive control present.
Randomised experimental study in 50 women with SUI. Experimental group performed 16 sessions of perineal exercises (PFMT); control group received no treatment. Inactive control.
Single‑blind RCT in 118 women with urodynamic SUI. PFMT, electrical stimulation, vaginal cones, and a no‑active‑treatment control. PFMT vs inactive control arm exists.
Prospective RCT in 130 women with stress and mixed UI. 12‑week home‑based PFMT versus a control group (no treatment). Inactive control.
RCT in 44 women with UI. Group behavioral modification program (including PFMT) versus a no‑treatment control group. PFMT vs inactive control present.

Abstract does not mention an inactive control group (no treatment, placebo, sham). It appears to compare different active physiotherapy modalities (medical gymnastics vs. electrical stimulation) without a valid inactive comparator, failing the control‑arm criterion.
Randomised crossover trial in 70 elderly women with stress UI. Multidimensional exercise class (including PFM exercises) versus control (no exercise during first period). Inactive control.
RCT in 147 elderly women with stress/urge/mixed UI. Exercise treatment (including PFMT) versus an education control group (inactive). PFMT vs inactive control.
RCT in 127 elderly women with stress, urge, mixed UI. Multidimensional exercise treatment (including PFMT) versus control (no exercise). Inactive control.
RCT in 55 older women with UI. Standardised physiotherapy programme (PFMT + behavioural therapy) versus control receiving advice/pamphlet (inactive).
RCT in 40 women with SUI. Physiotherapist‑supervised PFMT versus no treatment. Inactive control.
Randomised single‑blind study in 27 women with mild‑moderate SUI. Instruction in a pelvic floor pre‑contraction technique (form of PFMT) versus wait‑list control. Inactive control.
Pilot RCT in 49 women with SUI. PFMT (group or individual) versus a no‑treatment control group. Inactive control.
Pilot RCT in 34 women with MUI. PFMT arm versus a waiting‑list control. Inactive control.
RCT in 48 postmenopausal women with UI and osteoporosis. Weekly physical therapy for UI (including PFMT) versus osteoporosis education control (inactive).
RCT comparing pelvic muscle exercise (PFMT) and bladder training to a control group. PFMT vs inactive control present.
RCT in 75 women with SUI. Kinesitherapy (PFMT) group versus a control group (no treatment). Inactive control.
RCT in 32 volleyball athletes with SUI. Pelvic floor muscle rehabilitation programme (PFMRP) versus a pamphlet control (inactive).
RCT in 104 women with genuine stress incontinence. Pelvic floor exercises versus a no‑treatment control group. Inactive control present.
Randomised controlled trial in 66 women with genuine stress incontinence. Pelvic floor exercises versus no therapy control. Inactive control.
RCT in women with stress or mixed UI. One arm received PFMT, the other no treatment. Meets all criteria: population (SUI/MUI), intervention (PFMT), comparator (no treatment), design (RCT).

RCT of a nurse specialist involvement model versus usual care. This is a service delivery intervention, not a trial of PFMT versus inactive control. Does not meet the intervention/comparator criteria.
Satisfaction survey alongside the nurse specialist trial. Not itself an RCT, and the parent trial does not evaluate PFMT versus inactive control.

RCT in older women with urge/mixed UI comparing biofeedback-assisted behavioral training, verbal feedback behavioral training, and a self-help booklet. The self-help booklet is an active treatment, not an inactive control (no treatment, placebo, sham). Therefore the comparator does not meet the inclusion criteria.
Feasibility study, not described as a randomized controlled trial. Also the control group received an education session (active comparator), not an inactive control.
RCT comparing two forms of PFMT (supervised vs unsupervised). Both arms receive active PFMT; there is no inactive control arm.

RCT in women with chronic low back pain and stress UI, comparing stabilization exercises focusing on PFM versus routine physiotherapy. The control group receives active physiotherapy, not an inactive control. Also the population is not exclusively UI patients.
RCT in women with stress UI comparing behavioral training, behavioral training plus PFES, and a self-help booklet. The self-help booklet is an active treatment, not an inactive control.

RCT in elderly women with UI in long-term care. The intervention includes Kegel's exercises (PFMT). The control group is not explicitly described but is likely usual care/no treatment. Conservative inclusion – if the control is truly inactive, the study meets criteria.

RCT in women with UI. The intervention is behavioral therapy, which typically includes PFMT. The control group received no therapy (inactive). Meets population, intervention (PFMT component), and comparator criteria.

Economic evaluation alongside an RCT that compared two active PFMT arms (internet vs postal). No randomized inactive control arm in the trial; the no-treatment comparison was based on baseline data, not a randomized group.
RCT comparing internet-based PFMT versus postal PFMT. Both arms are active PFMT; there is no inactive control arm.
Long-term follow-up of the same trial; both arms active PFMT, no inactive control.

RCT in women with SUI comparing TA+PFM co-contraction exercises versus control. Control condition not described, but likely no treatment or sham. Conservative inclusion – if the control is inactive, the study meets criteria.

Pilot RCT in frail older women with UI. The intervention combines behavioral UI treatments (which include PFMT) with physical activity; the control is likely usual care/no treatment. Conservative inclusion – if the control is inactive, the study meets criteria.
Population is gynecologic cancer survivors with pelvic floor dysfunction, not explicitly women with SUI, UUI, or MUI. Does not meet the population criterion.
Psychometric study for questionnaire development and validation. Not a randomized controlled trial.
Systematic review, not an original RCT.
Systematic review, not an original RCT.

Review/discussion article. Not an RCT.

Instrument development/reproducibility study. Not an RCT.
Observational study using MRI to assess pelvic floor muscle function. Not an RCT, and not a treatment study.
Theoretical/discussion article on mechanisms of PFMT. Not an RCT.
Consensus terminology report; not a randomised trial. No intervention comparison of PFMT versus control.
Cross‑sectional survey (secondary analysis of EpiLUTS). No randomisation and no PFMT intervention.
Book chapter reviewing pharmacology of voiding disorders. Not a trial.
Narrative review of PFMT regimens; not a randomised trial itself.
Descriptive paper on FES. No controlled comparison, no PFMT arm.
Secondary analysis of data from healthy women (no UI at baseline); no control group, not a randomised trial.
Methodological guidance on GRADE SoF tables. Not a clinical trial.
Methodological guidance; not a randomised trial.
Population‑based prevalence survey; no intervention and no randomisation.
Consensus terminology report; not a trial.
Commentary on quality assessment in reviews; not a clinical trial.
Cross‑sectional study assessing quality of life. No intervention and no control group.
Systematic review and economic model, not a primary randomised trial.
Questionnaire development study; not a trial.
Survey of willingness‑to‑pay; not a randomised trial.
Cross‑sectional analysis of survey data. No intervention.
Questionnaire validation study; not a randomised trial.

The abstract states that participants were enrolled in a 25‑week longitudinal randomised control study testing a behavioural/educational intervention for urinary incontinence. Although PFMT is not explicitly named, the trial design (RCT) in women with incontinence and the possibility that the behavioural intervention could include PFMT warrant inclusion at the title/abstract screening stage. (low confidence)
Qualitative interview study to establish content validity of a questionnaire; not a trial.
Methodological study examining meta‑analyses; not a clinical trial.
Reporting guideline; not a trial.
Multi‑country survey; not a randomised controlled trial.
Descriptive study of pelvic muscle function in healthy continent nulliparous women; no UI, no randomisation, no control arm.
Validation of a severity index against pad‑weighing; not a randomised trial.
Cross‑sectional study comparing sexual function in women with and without incontinence. Not a trial.
Prospective cohort study evaluating a self-efficacy index; not a randomized or quasi-randomized controlled trial comparing PFMT to inactive control.
Measurement development paper for short form questionnaires; not a randomized controlled trial.
Development of a quality of life measure (I-QOL); not a randomized controlled trial.
Validation study of a quality of life scale in psoriasis patients; not about urinary incontinence and not an RCT.
Secondary analysis from duloxetine trials to validate global impression questionnaires; not a primary RCT comparing PFMT to inactive control.
Description of the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale development; not a trial and not about urinary incontinence.

Randomized controlled trial in obese perimenopausal women with stress urinary incontinence. One arm received PFMT; the control arm (not further specified) is likely no treatment or usual care, thus an inactive control. Meets inclusion criteria.

Randomized study in women with stress urinary incontinence comparing three groups: electrotherapy+PFMT, PFMT alone, and a control group. The PFMT alone vs control arm provides a relevant comparison of PFMT to an inactive control.
RCT evaluating acupressure (not PFMT) versus sham and usual care in women with urodynamic stress incontinence; no arm that is solely PFMT.
RCT comparing supervised plus home-based PFMT to home-based PFMT alone; no inactive control arm (both arms receive active PFMT).

RCT in women with SUI with four arms: combined (duloxetine+PFMT), PFMT alone, duloxetine alone, and no active treatment (imitation PFMT + placebo). The PFMT alone vs no active treatment arm meets the PFMT vs inactive control criterion.
Qualitative interview study nested within an RCT; not itself a randomized controlled trial.
Secondary analysis of predictors of success from a non-face-to-face treatment program; not a randomized controlled trial.
Systematic review title (Cochrane review), not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Review article summarizing exercise physiology and PFMT effectiveness; not a primary trial.
Anatomic/physiologic description article; not a randomized controlled trial.
Scale development and validation paper (Hopkins Symptom Checklist), not related to urinary incontinence or PFMT.
Book chapter or review on adult conservative management; not a primary RCT.
Methodological article about post-randomisation exclusions; not a trial.
Systematic review protocol or background section, not a primary RCT.
Communication on outcome measures for lower urinary tract dysfunction; not a trial.
Observational MRI cohort study, not a randomized controlled trial.

RCT compares urodynamic investigations prior to conservative treatment vs no prior urodynamics; both groups received active treatment (physiotherapy/bladder retraining), and the intervention is not PFMT. It does not compare PFMT to inactive control.
Cross-sectional clinical/physiologic study of pathophysiology in institutionalized elderly; not an RCT.
Cochrane review title, not a primary RCT.
